title: Numbers to 100
notes: An existing online family supplies only the pupil action it actually scores, not every claim in its feedback.
Concrete construction is our assessment design for digit meaning, not a separate compulsory EDB objective.
Zero-as-even is guidance in the explanatory notes, addressed here without turning an illustrative strategy into a new numbered objective.
No new global inventory or unit-closure claim made.

requirements.requirement: Count collections and recognise their totals
requirements.reviewNote: Oral teacher activity labels its activities by headings, not URL anchors; use the activity page and named section.

evidence.pupilAction: Write numeral from printed number words
C: write six dictated numerals, including 100

requirements.reviewNote: Dictation is an assessment mode, not another numbered objective.

evidence.pupilAction: Complete next value in forwards/backwards sequences
B: four spoken sequences crossing tens and reaching 100

requirements.requirement: Recognise odd/even through100, with explanatory guidance on zero

evidence.pupilAction: B: remove pairs 8 → 0, classify 0, 56, 73 and 100, identify relevant units digits

requirements.identifiedGapBeforeSupplement: Existing family has neither 0 nor 100, and only feedback explains the units rule.
requirements.reviewNote: Pupil demonstrates zero-even and gives a basis for two-digit decisions; teacher key accepts multiple representations.

objectives.summary: Recognise units and tens and the meanings of their digits

evidence.pupilAction: A: build 24, 42 and 60 using tens and singles

requirements.requirement: State or show the value of each digit, including zero ones

evidence.pupilAction: A:2 in 24 means 20; 4 means 4; 2 in 42 means 2; 0 in 60 records zero ones

requirements.identifiedGapBeforeSupplement: Existing family asks for total only; the meaning of the digit occurs in its worked key.
requirements.reviewNote: No need to use term place value; building is one means of showing understanding, not compulsory terminology.

evidence.pupilAction: Select larger number, including same-tens and 100 boundary

requirements.requirement: Order a group in either direction

evidence.pupilAction: Write three numerals in ascending or descending order

requirements.reviewNote: No inequality symbols; both directions included across 12 fixed cases.

objectives.summary: Count objects in groups of 2, 5 and 10

requirements.requirement: Count groupwise, below 100, without calculation notation

evidence.pupilAction: Count pictured groups and provide total
Optional group-counting section: successive totals for 24 in pairs, 35 in fives, 60 in tens

requirements.reviewNote: Oral evidence makes the process observable; use this section when assessing the objective, even though it is labelled optional on the general oral sheet.

requirements.requirement: Estimate below 100 using a reference after counting experience

evidence.pupilAction: Choose nearest offered ten from a pictured reference of 10 and target
C: estimate targets of 24 and 47 against a real reference of 10 before counting, explain reference use, then check

requirements.identifiedGapBeforeSupplement: Persistent digital dots permit exact counting; the answer alone does not establish estimation process.
requirements.reviewNote: Teacher records method and timing before counting; no invented EDB tolerance or nearest-ten requirement.

limits: Number-recognition range 21–100; zero parity addressed as explanatory extension
No multiplication expressions required for group counts
releaseGates: Independent content review of new activity and this map
Bilingual pupil/key route and toggle checks
Printing without key leakage or clipping
Check linked existing families and oral-sheet routes are live
Update objective inventory from actual reviewed evidence, leaving manual validation separately recorded
